permissions.reason: Inherited Ptyxis host/helper architecture currently carries development capability. Source and non-graphical CI do not prove that removing it preserves PTY, host-agent, process-monitoring, and container behavior.
Graphics acceleration is part of the packaged GTK/VTE rendering path. Removal requires real rendering, performance, transparency, fullscreen, and fallback validation.

This is the broadest filesystem grant and receives special scrutiny. Current Flathub Ptyxis carries the same permission, but its Flathub lint exception describes host-filesystem access as predating the rule rather than proving current necessity. GoreeCloud source review now supports an isolated development-only candidate that removes this permission, but supported-workstation behavior remains authoritative before any canonical manifest change.
IPC sharing is part of the inherited graphical Flatpak baseline and can affect X11/graphics integration. It must not be removed without graphical fallback and session validation.
GoreeCloud Terminal is required to support normal network-aware shell workflows including OpenSSH. Network access does not replace OpenSSH authentication or host-key authority.
The supported workstation acceptance model includes X11 fallback behavior. Removal is not justified until GoreeCloud explicitly drops that compatibility requirement or proves an alternate path.
Wayland is the primary graphical display path for the approved Linux workstation environment.

Current Ptyxis Flatpak architecture uses Flatpak host spawning for ptyxis-agent so PTY creation, host process monitoring, and container interaction can occur on the host. Flathub also records a lint exception identifying this access as required for ptyxis-agent PTY setup on the host.

source_findings: The Flatpak UI launches ptyxis-agent on the host through flatpak-spawn --host and org.freedesktop.Flatpak access.
The host-side session container validates the requested working directory with host-side filesystem checks before spawning the shell or command.
Command-line and preserved working directories are marshaled as URI/path metadata to the host-side spawn path instead of requiring the UI process to traverse the target directory.
External link opening uses the desktop portal.
Terminal drag and drop recognizes document-portal formats and can recover document-portal host-path metadata for shell insertion.
User palettes are stored under the application's XDG user-data directory rather than requiring unrestricted host filesystem visibility.

completion_rule: Permission minimization is incomplete until the supported workstation validates any proposed narrower manifest against all affected behaviors. Source review and CI alone cannot set permission_set_minimized true.
privacy_rule: Permission review evidence must not collect terminal contents, shell history, private SSH configuration, credentials, private keys, passwords, tokens, or unrelated host file contents.
